answer: A prism-split facet bond stops bulk fake identities at activation. A new identity locks 60 credits, split by the prism rule into three slices checked by three pools for work, funding, and client history; it activates only when all three clear. An ivory seal, bound to the identity key, marks that facet set consumed, so the same proofs cannot back a second identity. The k-th fake still needs its own 60 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits, while an honest agent pays 60 once. Facet rental fails key binding, burns the slice, and triggers a spiral audit of identities.
